analysis:
The PR changes only provider-swift/Sources/ProviderBenchmark/ThroughputSweep.swift, in the benchmark-only code path. Head lines 127, 219, 224, 227 and 237 make measurePrefill async throws. The two ctx.model.newCache(parameters:) calls (head 227 and 237) now use try, and the call site at head 127 uses try await. This follows an upstream API change, where newCache now throws. No other lines in the supplied head text differ from base, and the head unit shown ends at line 566, so the remainder is only the base text.

Security effect: errors from cache creation now propagate out of ThroughputSweep.run instead of being silently handled or never raised. The error path is fail-closed. It stays inside the offline benchmark tool and does not touch the coordinator-provider WebSocket (TB-002), attestation, App Attest authorization, key handling, or the encrypted SSD prefix cache (T-041). Prefill uses the model's own scalar caches with no KVCacheSSD interaction. The benchmark engine path passes constructionPurpose .benchmark with BenchmarkMemoryBudget and is unchanged.

No new data exposure, authorization change, or attack surface is identified. Remaining question for integration: the upstream protocol or model definition that makes newCache throw is outside the supplied evidence. I could not verify that other callers of newCache, including production serving paths, were updated consistently. That is a compile-time and availability concern, not a confirmed security regression.
